title: "IPPs: Political Integration and Contract Renegotiation"

**Andrew Wang and Hassan Aziz**

*Ongoing research · Accepted at APSA 2026*

[Code and data on GitHub](https://github.com/yuanzhouwang/ipps) · [All papers](research.html)

## Research question

Does Chinese sponsorship protect independent power producers (IPPs) in Pakistan from contract renegotiation? This project studies how foreign investment relationships sustain political commitments when formal institutional guarantees are weak.

The paper, **Foreign Political Integration: Chinese Sponsorship Reduces Renegotiation Hazard for Pakistani IPPs**, examines long-term power purchase agreements in Pakistan's energy sector, including projects associated with the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.

## Political integration

The theoretical framework draws on vertical political integration: coalitions linking governments, investors, and third-party enforcers can sustain investment relationships through political commitments. We examine whether ties to Chinese sponsors raise the costs of renegotiation and insulate firms from domestic fiscal and political pressure.

## Data and methods

The project combines original project-level data on sponsorship, plant capacity, and renegotiation events with source links and a Business Recorder news collection pipeline. The analysis uses Cox proportional hazards models to compare renegotiation risk across Chinese-sponsored and other IPPs while accounting for plant capacity, alongside a logit comparison.

The repository includes:

- A renegotiation dataset and R scripts for duration models, simulations, and plots.
- News scraping and article-processing tools, with dictionaries of IPP and group names and aliases.
- A working manuscript developing the political integration framework.

## Project status

Research and data collection are ongoing. Chinese sponsorship is the hypothesis under investigation; the current research summary reports null findings. The repository provides the analysis and its supporting materials for further development.
